text: Security is a vital part of web development. First, websites should use HTTPS to encrypt data between the user and the server, which protects sensitive information like passwords. Second, strong authentication, such as multi-factor login, helps confirm that users are who they claim to be. Third, developers must always validate input to stop harmful code from entering the system. Without these steps, sites remain open to common vulnerabilities such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. These attacks are common and can seriously damage users and businesses. By applying HTTPS, careful authentication, and input validation, developers can reduce these risks and build safer, more trustworthy websites.
